citations.assessment: The Baraita explicitly gives R. Yehudah’s story of ben Nappaḥa’s five courtyards at Usha. It leaves the name’s origin open.

holds.raw: וצ"ע כי נראה נפחא שם עיר
holds.reason: The Eruvin incident locates the five courtyards at Usha and styles the person ben Nappaḥa. It does not identify any town named Nappaḥa or prove the patronymic explanation.

notes.text: Ḥullin prints Yitzḥak bar Nappaḥa. Heilprin’s separate Yitzḥak entry judges the bar form there a scribal error, making it important to preserve the objection in this entry as a separate voice.
